The library maps buttons, not modifier keys, so the file converts each Ctrl+primary pointer event into a synthetic right-button event on the canvas. The camera's existing pan path then handles it, so sensitivity and glide match a right-drag. Plain primary drags, touch, and wheel/pinch go to the library's normal controls, and the returned cleanup removes every listener and detaches the controls. I could not run or type-check this, because the library isn't on this machine.

- **Root export:** I assumed `attachControl` is exported from `"@babylonjs/lite"`. The declarations don't show the package index.
- **Build config:** `tsconfig.json` maps `@babylonjs/lite` to `../babylon-lite/packages/babylon-lite/src/index.ts`, which is outside `app/`. Type-checking will fail until that path exists.
